title: The Shepherd and the Wolf

sentences.text: A shepherd watched a flock of sheep on a green hill above a village.
The work was quiet, and the shepherd grew bored.
One afternoon the shepherd shouted, Wolf! Wolf! toward the houses.
Neighbors dropped their tools and ran up the hill to help.
There was no wolf. The sheep were grazing, and the shepherd was laughing.
The neighbors frowned and walked back down the path.
The next day the shepherd tried the joke again, and again the neighbors came.
They were angry this time, and they warned the shepherd not to call unless a wolf was real.
That evening a real wolf crept out of the trees.
The shepherd shouted for help, louder than before.
Down in the village, people heard the cry and shook their heads.
It is only another joke, they said, and nobody climbed the hill.
The wolf rushed the flock and scattered the sheep across the slope.
The shepherd gathered them again much later, with shaking hands.
A joke that is a lie can make the truth hard to believe.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: A false alarm that makes a real alarm hard to believe
A wolf who learns to guard a flock
Neighbors who move the village uphill
A shepherd who builds a taller fence

questions.explanation: The shepherd calls for help when there is no wolf. Later a real wolf comes, and nobody believes the call. That loss of trust is the main idea.

questions.prompt: What do the neighbors do the first time they hear the shout?

choices.text: They lock every door in the village
They run up the hill to help
They laugh and stay where they are
They send the wolf back to the trees

questions.explanation: The first time, the neighbors drop their tools and run up the hill. They only refuse to come after the joke has been repeated.

questions.prompt: How does the shepherd most likely feel while gathering the sheep?

choices.text: Proud that the joke worked again
Shaken, and sorry the joke was told
Sure the neighbors are still laughing

questions.explanation: The story does not say the word sorry. Shaking hands, a scattered flock, and neighbors who would not come are clues that the shepherd feels upset, not proud.

choices.text: The shepherd shouts the first false alarm
Neighbors warn that the joke must stop
A real wolf comes out of the trees
The shepherd gathers the sheep again

questions.explanation: The false alarms come first, then the warning, then the real wolf. The last action is the shepherd gathering the sheep much later.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
